chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from his father and ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
Concerning a woman who becomes pure at the beginning of the day in Ramaḍān: does she break the fast or fast? He said: “She breaks the fast.”

And concerning a woman who sees blood at the beginning of the day in the month of Ramaḍān: does she break the fast or fast? He said: “She breaks the fast; rather, her breaking of the fast is due to the blood.”

His statement عليه السلام, “rather, her breaking of the fast is due to the blood,” indicates that even if she does not break the fast by food and drink, she is nevertheless under the ruling of one who has broken the fast. Then he said: it is forbidden for her husband to have intercourse with her until she has emerged from menstruation.
This is indicated by His, Exalted is He, saying:
“And they ask you about menstruation. Say: it is a hurt, so keep away from women during menstruation and do not approach them until they become pure.”
Thus, by this wording, He prohibited approaching them and made avoiding them obligatory until they become pure. This is apparent, and it also indicates it.

key_terms.الدَّمِ: menstrual blood that determines the legal ruling here
key_terms.الْمَحِيضِ: the state or time of menstruation mentioned in the Qur'an
key_terms.الْمُفْطِرَةِ: one judged to have broken the fast
key_terms.تُفْطِرُ: breaks the fast or is ruled as not fasting

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting and marital relations when menstruation begins or ends during the day in Ramaḍān?
ai.summary: This passage gives a legal ruling on menstruation in relation to fasting in Ramaḍān and marital relations. It states that the onset or cessation of menstrual blood determines the ruling of fasting for that day, and it cites the Qur'an to establish the prohibition of intercourse during menstruation until purification.
